picks.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy
picks.rationale: UCLA optical (light-based) AI screens a dozen-plus videos at once for deepfakes at ~98% accuracy and low energy; a new hardware method with broad relevance.
picks.excerpt: UCLA researchers built an optical AI system that uses light to analyze more than a dozen videos at once, detecting deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy at low energy cost and with resistance to adversarial attacks.

picks.title: AI's failed attempt to crack the Riemann hypothesis led a mathematician to a breakthrough
picks.rationale: First-person account of Claude's failed Riemann attempt that still sparked a real result; a fresh angle on AI in mathematics that is distinct from the earlier curve, sphere and probability stories.
picks.excerpt: An attempt by Anthropic's Claude failed to prove the Riemann hypothesis, but it did produce something genuinely useful: inspiration.

picks.title: This game-playing AI is the new champ at Stratego
picks.rationale: MIT system beats human experts at the hidden-information game Stratego more cheaply than larger models, a step toward AI that supports decisions under uncertainty.
picks.excerpt: Researchers developed an AI system that beat human experts at the board wargame Stratego and outperformed more expensive models. This new system could someday help humans make strategic decisions in situations when some information is hidden.

picks.title: Forecasting space weather risks on power grids
picks.rationale: ML system predicts where geomagnetic storms will damage power grids 30-60 minutes ahead; new space-weather application, distinct from the published hurricane-intensity story.
picks.excerpt: Extreme space-weather events can damage power systems on Earth and degrade GPS accuracy and satellite operations. A new machine learning system can predict where damage is likely to occur 30-60 minutes before a storm arrives.

picks.title: Adaptive AI boosts math only slightly; the human teacher remains essential
picks.rationale: Three-year study of ~8,000 Dutch pupils gives hard evidence on adaptive AI learning systems in classrooms: modest arithmetic gains, and the teacher is still essential.
picks.excerpt: A three-year study of nearly 8,000 Dutch elementary pupils found adaptive AI learning systems modestly improved arithmetic performance, but researchers stress the human teacher remains essential.
